title: Intervention
description: Act one's two orderings. Generated by scripts/build_intervention.py from the campaign's per-pair attribution and patching records, joined exactly on (dimension, pair_id). Consumed by components/intervention-panel on /see/reward-model/ section 3 and by the reduced form on the homepage. Every value is a measurement; the contract's rule is that nothing in this panel is a simulation, so there is no interpolation, no modelled component and no fallback. THE MOVEMENT AXIS IS NOT BOUNDED BY 100%: patching noises a component's activations, so the margin can invert and overshoot, and `patchFractionOfMargin` reaches 7.71 on this subject. A renderer that clamps, winsorises or renormalises it hides the most surprising values in the set.

headline.description: The figures three routes state in prose: the homepage's mechanism paragraphs, its first figure, and /log/ section 4. Read out of the E-parity fixture and out of the project's own correction note. Nothing here is a second copy of `dimensions`: the mean is the fixture's published per-model mean, not an average of the twelve.

meanRho.description: The published per-model mean rank correlation for the canonical model.

sharpestDimension.description: The dimension with the most negative correlation. Derived from `dimensions`, never named here.

toleranceStated.description: The fixture's own stated tolerance for these values.

correction.description: The one place on this site where the superseded value is rendered on purpose. /log/ section 4's subject is that the project published a correlation, checked it against its own fixtures, found it wrong and said so. Both numbers are parsed out of the correction note, so the section cannot become a hand-typed account of a correction.

deprecatedRho.description: The withdrawn value. It is quoted here and nowhere else, and gate 7's number allow-list has to say so.

supersedingRhoAsQuoted.description: The replacing value AS THE CORRECTION NOTE WRITES IT, to three places. `meanRho` above is the same quantity at the fixture's full precision, and the generator fails if the two disagree beyond the note's own rounding. The correction sentence quotes the note; a figure axis uses `meanRho`.

subject.description: The full model identifier. A third-party artifact name, permitted in rendered output.

pairSource.description: The pair set every row came from, as the record names it. An internal identifier: not for rendered prose.

patchedComponentCount.description: Smaller than the attributed count, and the difference is named in `unpatchedComponents` rather than dropped. The panel fails the build on a component holding one rank and not the other, so a component the study did not patch is not in `components` at all.

unpatchedComponents.description: Attributed and never patched. Rendered nowhere, stated here so the 64-of-65 is visible rather than looking like a miscount.

patchingMode.description: Which intervention produced `patchEffect`. Recorded because a patch effect means nothing without it.

evidenceId.description: Null. These numbers predate the evidence store and resolve to a cached experiment output rather than to a record, so DECISIONS.md D-35 applies: `derivedFrom` carries the file and its content hash in place of an id, and no id is minted.

sha256.description: A content hash rather than a line number: the source is a 360-row record and no single line carries an aggregate.

nullThreshold.description: A SPECIFICATION VALUE, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and the only one in this file. components/intervention-panel.md defines it as a prop default and its acceptance criterion 10 forbids the implementation hardcoding a threshold, so it is carried here with the line it is written on. Below this absolute relative movement the panel renders its null-state hint. It is a displayed threshold and never a filter: no component is hidden by it.

dimensions.description: One objective dimension per entry, in a stable order. Each is a complete panel instance.

pairCount.description: Preference pairs behind every mean on this dimension.

spearmanRho.description: The published per-dimension rank correlation between attribution magnitude and patch-effect magnitude, taken from the E-parity fixture rather than recomputed. It is a mean of PER-PAIR correlations and is therefore not the correlation of the two aggregate orderings in `components`; those are different statistics and must not be presented as the same number.

marginMean.description: Mean unpatched reward differential over this dimension's pairs, signed. The panel's original score.

marginMeanAbsolute.description: Mean magnitude of the same quantity. Not the denominator of `patchFractionOfMargin`, which is taken per pair; stated so a reader can see how far the two differ.

negativeMargins.description: Pairs on this dimension where the model preferred the dispreferred completion. Non-zero is why the fraction is taken against the magnitude per pair rather than against a dimension-level mean.

components.description: Every patched component, in a stable order. The panel sorts by `attributionRank` for one list and `patchRank` for the other, and sorting either by anything else destroys the finding. A components array shorter than two fails the build: one ranking cannot disagree with itself.

patchRank.description: 1 is the largest patch-effect magnitude. The disagreement between this and attributionRank is the act's finding.

attributionValue.description: Mean magnitude of this component's differential contribution. A magnitude because that is what the experiment correlates and what the library's own ranking uses.

patchEffect.description: Mean magnitude of the change patching this component makes to the reward differential, in the model's own reward units.

patchFractionOfMargin.description: The same movement as a fraction of the pair's own margin, averaged over the dimension's pairs. NOT BOUNDED ABOVE BY 1. Values above 1 mean patching moved the score further than the whole preference margin, and they are real: the largest on this subject is 7.71. Do not clamp, winsorise or renormalise.

patchFractionOfMarginSigned.description: The library's own `PatchResult.normalized_effects`, averaged: patch effect over margin, keeping the sign. Positive means patching shrank the margin, because the library defines the effect as original minus patched. The panel announces a SIGNED percentage, so this is the one it announces; `patchFractionOfMargin` is the one it draws.

evidenceId.description: Null, for the reason on meta.evidenceId. The panel renders the file citation at the weight a provenance chip would get rather than levelling the difference.

citation.description: DECISIONS.md D-35's shape: where a number was resolved when it is not in the evidence store. A reader opens the document at the line and reads it.
